title: Adaptive backoff + typed pagination for embeddings client (Python/TS)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current embeddings client has brittle pagination semantics and a one-size-fits-all retry/backoff strategy. Customers building reranking pipelines observe high tail latency and duplicate work when transient network errors or partial stream disconnects occur. We need a client-side design that reduces unnecessary retries, provides deterministic typed responses for downstream static typing (Python dataclasses / TS generics), and offers a clear, ergonomic pagination iterator for both sync and async users.
background: Existing tickets (ENG-4821, ENG-9034, ENG-17190, ENG-26540) improved pagination ergonomics and typed responses in parts, but there remain gaps: 1) backoff strategy is static and causes burst retries against the inference layer; 2) cursor tokens are opaque strings with no schema guarantees; 3) Python/TS parity is inconsistent (sync iterator in Python vs async-only patterns in TS) and 4) error surface is not typed, making consumer code brittle for reranking pipelines that need granular handling for 'partial-results' vs 'hard-failure'.
goals: Implement adaptive exponential backoff with jitter and server-guided hints to reduce client retry storms
Add a strongly typed pagination iterator surface in Python (sync + async) and TypeScript (async iterator + helper sync wrapper for Node sync callers)
Define and validate a minimal cursor schema (versioned) to prevent accidental breaking changes across server rollouts
Introduce specific error classes/types (e.g., EmbeddingsPartialResultError, EmbeddingsRateLimitError, EmbeddingsTransientError) and surface them in both SDKs
Preserve backwards compatibility for simple usage while enabling advanced knobs for PL/infra customers
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a PaginationIterator with next_page() / __anext__ semantics returning TypedEmbeddingPage objects (docs + type hints) in both Python and TS
Clients implement adaptive backoff: base=100ms, max=5s, jitter=full; server may return 'retry_after_ms' in 429/503 with override up to 30s
Cursor token includes a 1-byte version and a base64 payload; SDK validates version and raises a descriptive error if unsupported
Define and ship three typed error classes in both SDKs and update docs with example handling patterns for reranking loops
Performance: tail-latency (95th percentile) for paginated embedding streams reduced by >=15% in our internal load test compared to baseline without adaptive backoff
Add SDK metrics for retries, backoff events, cursor decodes failures reported to telemetry; tests and docs included
Migration guide added: code snippets for switching from legacy pagination to the new iterator and error types
implementation_plan: Design: finalize cursor schema and error taxonomy (owner: Diego) — 2d
Server: add optional 'retry_after_ms' field on error envelope and cursor version header (owner: infra) — 3d
Python SDK: implement SyncPaginationIterator and AsyncPaginationIterator, dataclass TypedEmbeddingPage, typed exceptions, unit tests (owner: Priya) — 5d
TS SDK: implement AsyncIterator + utility for synchronous callers, generics for TypedEmbeddingPage<T>, typed exceptions, unit tests (owner: Tomas) — 6d
E2E: create a load test harness with transient error injection to validate backoff and tail-latency improvements (owner: SRE) — 3d
Docs: migration guide, examples for reranking loop, best-practices for batch sizing and retry policies (owner: Docs) — 2d
Rollout: staged release behind feature flag; monitor telemetry and disable if retry storm detected (owner: release)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clients may misconfigure aggressive max_retries leading to increased load. Mitigation: sensible defaults, feature-flagged opt-in for non-default policies, telemetry alarms
Risk: Cursor schema change could break older clients. Mitigation: add version byte and graceful error with migration hints, server to accept old cursors during rollout
Risk: Additional metric volume from client telemetry. Mitigation: sample telemetry by default and allow higher sampling via env/config for enterprise customers
Risk: Type drift across languages. Mitigation: share canonical JSON schema in repo and generate TS types and Python pydantic/dataclass bindings as part of CI
tests: Unit tests for pagination iterator covering normal flow, empty pages, and final page
Simulated network failures to assert backoff trajectories and de-duplication of completed pages
Integration tests between SDK and server feature-flagged retry_after_ms behavior
Contract tests validating cursor encode/decode across SDKs (round-trip)
Load test comparing baseline vs adaptive backoff under injected 429/503 errors
telemetry_and_observability: Span attributes for SDK traces: page_size, cursor_version, retry_reason, server_retry_after_ms
Dashboards: add a page to Console 'Embeddings SDK' showing retry rate and cursor failures per client version
migration_notes: Existing users can continue using current cursor tokens; the new SDK will prefer new cursor schema but accept old tokens if server-side compatibility flag is enabled. Documented code snippets show migration path and feature-flag toggles. Recommend customers pin SDK minor versions during migration window.
open_questions: Should we expose max_backoff configurable in public SDKs or hide behind advanced config? (trade-off: simplicity vs enterprise control)
What sampling rate for client telemetry should be default for free-tier customers? (privacy/cost tradeoff)
Do we need a server-side deduplication token for paginated items to handle at-least-once semantics under retries?
comments: 2026-03-02 — Priya (Eng): POC of SyncPaginationIterator is done; it returns dataclass TypedEmbeddingPage with 'items' and 'cursor'. Saw a subtle race when a server returns a new cursor while previous stream is still being processed.

2026-03-04 — Anika (PM): Customer impact note — Top enterprise customers asked for deterministic error classes so their reranking loops don't collapse into generic retry logic. Prioritize typing and migration docs.
2026-03-06 — Tomas (TS Eng): TS generic implementation covers T for embedding payload. Need to sync on exception names to match Python exactly for support docs.
2026-03-09 — SRE: Load tests show 18% improvement on 95th pct when adaptive backoff enabled with server retry_after present. Pushing for staged rollout to 10% of traffic first.
